newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end higher on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end higher on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Singapore shares staged a mild recovery on Wednesday afternoon, as small-scale bargain-hunting for cheap blue chips counteracted fears of gloomy economic news.
Both the unweighted Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) and the more representative DBS-50 index rallied in late trade on the back of rises in a range of large industrial stocks.
The STII closed up 22.04 points at 2084.02 while the DBS-50 finished 5.70 points higher at 528.31.
Food group Cerebos, drinks firm Fraser & Neave and maritime based Keppel Corp all rose between 20 and 60 cents to end at Singapore $10.90, S$14.10 and S$10.60 respectively.
Dealers said the late rally was unexpected and noted that it was accomplished on very low volume of just 88.6 million shares.
"The index is still yo-yoing," said one dealer. "I wouldn't read too much into this."
He said foreign funds were largely staying away from the Singapore market for fear of more bad economic news.
The city-state has published a series of figures showing falls in exports in recent months and is expected to announce soon that its economy grew only two or three percent in the third quarter.
